mainTopic: The sources for liability when offering a blemished animal (קבלת הדם and זריקה), and why consecrating a blemished animal brings מלקות
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a פסוק was needed to teach that one gets מלקות for consecrating a blemished animal even after the גורל of יום כיפור. Then רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says one is also liable for collecting the blood (קבלת הדם) of a blemished animal. The גמרא works out which פסוק teaches which act: 'לא תקריבו' in ויקרא 22:24, 'על המזבח', and 'ומיד בן נכר לא תקריבו' in ויקרא 22:25. It does this in two versions, and in both רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ends up learning קבלת הדם from 'ומיד בן נכר'. The רבנן use that פסוק instead to teach that we do not accept blemished offerings from non-Jews. Next, ריש לקיש suggests the איסור applies only to an animal that became blemished later, since one blemished from birth is like a date palm. רבי יוחנן proves from the count of five prohibitions that the איסור covers born-blemished animals too, and explains that choosing a blemished animal over perfect ones is a disgrace. Based on this reason, רבא rules that one is lashed even when consecrating a blemished animal for the money of נסכים. A ברייתא supporting רבא is introduced, and its words come on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the verse was needed for the case after the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we needed a פסוק to teach that one gets מלקות even after the גורל. Without it, we might think that once it is clear which goat is 'for ה'', consecrating a blemished one as the other goat brings no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: before the lottery, we don't know which animal will become the one for ה', so he is flogged. But here, once it is already clear which one is for ה', maybe he is not flogged. So the verse comes to teach us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why a פסוק was needed. It shows a mistaken idea we might have had, and says the פסוק comes to correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גורל, any animal might end up as the one offered to ה', so making a blemished one holy is clearly a problem. After the גורל, it is already known that this animal is not the one offered to ה'. We might have thought there are no מלקות then, so the פסוק teaches that he is still flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind to say (a mistaken idea the גמרא is about to reject)
Fixed as the one for ה' (decided by the lottery)
It is recognizable / already clear
He receives מלקות (lashes)
It comes to teach us (the point of the source)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the goat sent away after the גורל has no holiness rules at all. The גמרא is only saying we might have thought there are no מלקות in this specific case, and the פסוק teaches that there are.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
Granted, at the start we do not know
whether this one will be fixed for the Name,
phrases.notes: 'The Name' means ה'. He's asking whether the lottery will pick this goat as the one offered to ה'.

phrases.english: but here, since it is already clear which is for the Name,
he is not flogged;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about why a פסוק was needed for the case after the lottery.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken idea that makes the פסוק necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once it is clear which goat is for ה', consecrating a blemished animal as the other goat brings no מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that he is flogged even after the lottery.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view on collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier statement that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds קבלת הדם to the list of acts that bring מלקות. It then asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, also collecting the blood brings liability. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes an earlier ruling and asks where its source is. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list of liable acts with a blemished animal did not include collecting the blood. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds it, so the גמרא wants a פסוק that supports this extra item.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood of the קרבן in a holy vessel
What is the reason? (asking for a source)
Also / even

phrases.english: The Master said:
In the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
also for the collection of the blood.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting an earlier ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that tells רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that collecting the blood brings liability.

steps.title: The source: the extra words in the verse about damaged animals
steps.stepSummary: The source is ויקרא 22:24. Its words 'לא תקריבו לה'' are extra, since an earlier פסוק already forbade offering a blemished animal. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses them for קבלת הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'bruised, crushed, torn, or cut, etc. (do not offer to ה')'. This refers to collecting the blood, which רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. Its extra words are read as forbidding the collection of the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already said in 22:20 not to offer any blemished animal. So the repeated 'לא תקריבו' in 22:24 must teach something new, and for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that new thing is קבלת הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Bruised and crushed (blemishes of the testicles)
Torn and cut off

phrases.english: The verse says:
"That which is bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:24. The 'etc.' points to the end of the פסוק, 'לא תקריבו לה'', which is the extra phrase being used here.

phrases.english: this is the collection of the blood,
which Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda spoke of.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'לא תקריבו' in ויקרא 22:24 teaches liability for קבלת הדם.

steps.title: What does the תנא קמא do with the extra words?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא does not hold that one is liable for collecting the blood. So the גמרא asks what he learns from the extra 'לא תקריבו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the תנא קמא, why do I need this 'you shall not offer'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the other opinion. If the extra words are not for קבלת הדם, what are they for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general rule is that the Torah does not add words for nothing. If the תנא קמא disagrees about קבלת הדם, he still needs some use for this extra phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, whose view is stated first in the ברייתא
Why do I need it? (the words seem extra)
You shall not offer

phrases.english: And according to the first Tanna,
why do I need this "you shall not offer"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא, הַאי לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the source from step 3 against the opposing opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra phrase must teach something, and the תנא קמא does not use it for קבלת הדם.

steps.title: The תנא קמא uses it for sprinkling the blood
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses the extra words to teach liability for sprinkling the blood (זריקת דמים).
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for sprinkling the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא learns a different law from the same extra words: sprinkling the blood on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the phrase is extra. They only argue about what it teaches: collecting the blood (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה) or sprinkling it (תנא קמא).

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different law)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: He needs it for the sprinkling of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִזְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra phrase a different use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase has no use for the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא it teaches liability for זריקת דמים.

steps.title: But sprinkling is already learned from 'on the altar'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the תנא קמא should already know about sprinkling from the words 'על המזבח' in an earlier פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he already learns that from 'on the altar'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 5. Sprinkling seems to be covered by a different פסוק, so it can't be the reason for the extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 22:22 says not to put any part of such an animal 'on the altar', which would include the blood. If so, sprinkling is already forbidden, and 'לא תקריבו' would be extra again.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (from another source)
On the altar
But surely (opening a challenge)

phrases.english: But surely he derives this from "on the altar"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:22

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לא תקריבו' is needed for זריקת דמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling already comes from 'על המזבח', so there is no need for another source.

steps.title: 'On the altar' is just how the verse speaks
steps.stepSummary: For the תנא קמא, 'על המזבח' teaches nothing extra; it is just the normal way the פסוק talks. So sprinkling must come from 'לא תקריבו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is just the way the verse speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'על המזבח' are just normal wording, not a source for a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every word in a פסוק is used to teach a new law; sometimes it just describes things in the usual way. Since 'על המזבח' teaches nothing, the תנא קמא needs 'לא תקריבו' to teach זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way of the פסוק (wording, not a new law)
Speaks / expresses itself

phrases.english: It is the way of the verse to speak like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹרְחֵיהּ דִּקְרָא דְּמִשְׁתַּעֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the competing phrase as plain wording, not a source for a law
steps.terutzMaskana: 'על המזבח' is just how the פסוק talks, so sprinkling is learned from 'לא תקריבו'.

steps.title: Shouldn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also read it as plain wording?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: doesn't רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also agree that 'על המזבח' is just the way the פסוק talks? If so, he too needs 'לא תקריבו' for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה too, isn't it just the way of the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same reasoning back onto רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. This threatens his source for collecting the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'על המזבח' is just wording for him as well, then 'לא תקריבו' is needed for זריקה. That would leave him with no source for קבלת הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Also / too
It is (here asking: isn't it?)

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda too,
isn't it just the way of the verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי, אוֹרְחֵיהּ דִּקְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 7 to the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה given in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he also reads 'על המזבח' as plain wording, 'לא תקריבו' goes to זריקה and is no longer free for קבלת הדם.

steps.title: Yes, he agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also reads 'על המזבח' as plain wording, so he too uses 'לא תקריבו' for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge instead of pushing it away. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also learns sprinkling from 'לא תקריבו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes back the source given in step 3 for קבלת הדם. It opens a new question: where does he learn קבלת הדם from now?

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (accepting a point)

steps.confusionAlert: This 'yes' means the source from step 3 is dropped for קבלת הדם. The extra 'לא תקריבו' now teaches זריקה for both opinions.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses 'לא תקריבו' in 22:24 for קבלת הדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses it for זריקה, like the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Then where does he learn collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: Since 'לא תקריבו' in 22:24 now goes to sprinkling, the גמרא asks for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's new source for קבלת הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then where does he learn collecting the blood from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a new source, because the old one was just taken away. It is setting up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling about קבלת הדם still stands. Only its source has to be replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: Then / rather (moving on after accepting a point)
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: Then from where does he learn collection of the blood?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קַבָּלַת הַדָּם מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from what step 9 accepted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A new פסוק that teaches liability for קבלת הדם.

steps.title: The new source: 'From the hand of a foreigner you shall not offer'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns קבלת הדם from ויקרא 22:25, 'ומיד בן נכר לא תקריבו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from this: 'And from the hand of a foreigner you shall not offer.' This is the collection of the blood that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה spoke of.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source for collecting the blood: the 'לא תקריבו' in the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each 'לא תקריבו' has its own job. The one in 22:24 teaches זריקה (for both opinions), and the one in 22:25 teaches קבלת הדם (for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה).

keyTerms.meaning: From the hand of
A foreigner (a non-Jew)

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions learn זריקת דמים from 'לא תקריבו' in ויקרא 22:24, and both read 'על המזבח' as plain wording. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also holds one is liable for קבלת הדם, which he learns from 'ומיד בן נכר לא תקריבו' (22:25).

phrases.english: He learns it from this:
"And from the hand of a foreigner you shall not offer"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:25

phrases.english: this is the collection of the blood
which Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda spoke of.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבלת הדם is learned from 'ומיד בן נכר לא תקריבו' (ויקרא 22:25).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 22:24 teaches זריקה and 22:25 teaches קבלת הדם.

steps.title: Why does the first opinion need the verse about a foreigner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנא קמא learns from 'ומיד בן נכר לא תקריבו', since he does not use it for קבלת הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the תנא קמא, why do I need this 'you shall not offer'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the תנא קמא. It asks what he does with the פסוק that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה just used for קבלת הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה used ויקרא 22:25 for קבלת הדם. The תנא קמא does not give a punishment for קבלת הדם, so this פסוק looks unused for him. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Why do I need it? (What does this teach?)
You shall not offer

phrases.english: And according to the first tanna,
why do I need this 'you shall not offer'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:25, the 'ומיד בן נכר' פסוק from step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתַנָּא קַמָּא, הַאי ״לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the same פסוק from step 11, this time from the side of the תנא קמא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא learns from ויקרא 22:25.

steps.title: The verse forbids a non-Jew to offer a blemished animal on our altar
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses the פסוק to teach that a בן נח may not offer a blemished animal on the מזבח in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for this: You might have thought that since בני נח were only commanded about an animal missing a limb, it makes no difference whether they offer on their own altar or on our altar. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק teaches a separate rule. A non-Jew may not bring a blemished animal on our מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני נח are only forbidden to offer a מחוסר אבר, an animal missing a limb. Other blemishes are allowed for them. We might have thought the same lenient rule applies even when they offer on the Jewish מזבח, so the פסוק 'מיד בן נכר' tells us it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say
Non-Jews, descendants of נח
An animal missing a limb
So it teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: For the תנא קמא, 'מיד בן נכר' is not about קבלת הדם. It forbids a non-Jew to bring a blemished animal on our מזבח.

phrases.english: He needs it for this:
It would enter your mind to say,
since the descendants of Noah were not commanded
except about an animal missing limbs,
there is no difference whether on their altar
or on our altar,
phrases.notes: 'Our altar' means the מזבח in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that a בן נח may not offer a blemished animal on the Jewish מזבח.

steps.title: Second version: רבי יוסי includes collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: A לישנא אחרינא begins. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says there is a prohibition for קבלת הדם too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: also for collecting the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the whole discussion. It opens again with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view that קבלת הדם of a blemished animal is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is the same as before. What changes in this version is which פסוקים are used for which act, as the next steps will show.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version (of the discussion)
Catching the animal's blood in a holy vessel

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is a second telling of the same סוגיא, and in it the פסוקים are matched to the acts differently.

phrases.english: Another version:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Also for the collection of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second version of the discussion found in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a prohibition on קבלת הדם of a blemished animal.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which פסוק רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses in this second version. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the source, not the ruling. The answer will show how this version divides the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason/source?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling.

steps.title: 'Bruised... shall not offer' is collecting; sprinkling is from 'on the altar'
steps.stepSummary: In this version, 'ומעוך... לא תקריבו' teaches קבלת הדם, and 'על המזבח' teaches זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Bruised or crushed... you shall not offer.' This is קבלת הדם. And he learns זריקה from 'on the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's sources in this version. ויקרא 22:24 is for קבלה, and 'על המזבח' is for זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the first version. There, 'על המזבח' was just the normal way the פסוק talks, and 22:24 was used for זריקה. Here, 'על המזבח' teaches זריקה, which leaves 22:24 free for קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
He derives it
Bruised and crushed (blemishes of the testicles)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Bruised or crushed... you shall not offer'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:24

phrases.english: this is the collection of the blood,
and sprinkling he derives
from 'on the altar.'

steps.title: The רבנן should also learn sprinkling from 'on the altar'

steps.simpleTranslation: And for the רבנן too, let them learn זריקה from 'on the altar'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If 'על המזבח' teaches זריקה, then the רבנן should learn it from there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן also learn זריקה from 'על המזבח', then 'ומעוך... לא תקריבו' has no job for them. They do not use it for קבלה either. So what does the extra wording teach them?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (here, the תנא קמא)

steps.kashyaTarget: How the רבנן use the פסוקים in the second version.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'על המזבח' is the source for זריקה, the רבנן should use it too, and then 22:24 would have no purpose for them.

steps.title: Yes, and 'Bruised' teaches about a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the רבנן learn זריקה from 'על המזבח'. It says they use 'ומעוך... לא תקריבו' for a במת יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is so. Then what does 'you shall not offer' of 'bruised' come for? We use it for a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It then finds a different job for 22:24: it forbids offering a blemished animal even on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do learn זריקה from 'על המזבח'. The words 'לא תקריבו' in 22:24 are not wasted. They extend the prohibition to a במת יחיד, a private altar that was allowed at times when there was no בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so

steps.title: רבי יוסי also needs 'Bruised' for a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה also needs 22:24 for a במת יחיד, so how can he use it for קבלה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, doesn't he need this for a private altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same point against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. If 22:24 is needed for a במת יחיד, it cannot also be his source for קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone needs a source for the rule about a במת יחיד. Once 22:24 goes there, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה has lost his source for קבלת הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for another teaching)

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
doesn't he need this for a private altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְבָמַת יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 18 back to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source for קבלה in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 22:24 is needed for a במת יחיד, so it cannot also teach קבלה.

steps.title: Yes, so he learns collecting from 'from the hand of a foreigner'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees, and says רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns קבלת הדם from 'מיד בן נכר לא תקריבו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is so. Then where does he get 'you shall offer' for קבלה? From 'Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall you offer.' This is קבלת הדם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that 22:24 is for a במת יחיד. It then gives רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה a new source for קבלה: ויקרא 22:25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second version ends at the same place as the first. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns קבלת הדם from 'מיד בן נכר'. Only the path to get there is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed so
From where does he learn it?
A foreigner, a non-Jew

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ends up learning קבלת הדם from 'מיד בן נכר לא תקריבו' (ויקרא 22:25).

phrases.english: Yes, indeed so,
but from where does he get 'you shall offer' for collection?
'Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall you offer'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:25

phrases.english: this is the collection of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא ״תַּקְרִיבוּ״ דְּקַבָּלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 19 and gives a new source for קבלה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge and moves to a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 22:24 was רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source for קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 22:24 teaches a במת יחיד, and 22:25 teaches קבלת הדם.

steps.title: The רבנן need 'מכל אלה' to teach that we do not accept blemished offerings from non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the פסוק 'מיד בן נכר... מכל אלה' to teach that we do not accept blemished animals from a נכרי. Without it, we might have thought we could, since בני נח are only commanded about a מחוסר אבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן need this פסוק for something else. You might have thought: since בני נח are only commanded not to offer an animal missing a limb on their own altars, maybe we can also accept blemished animals from them. So the פסוק says 'of any of these' to teach that we do not accept them.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 20 showed that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses 'מיד בן נכר לא תקריבו' for קבלת הדם. Now the גמרא explains what the רבנן use that פסוק for, since they do not hold that one is liable for קבלה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני נח may offer an animal with a small blemish. The only animal they may not offer is a מחוסר אבר. So one might think the Temple can take such animals from them too. The words 'מכל אלה' teach that every blemish disqualifies an animal brought by a נכרי, just as it does for a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of נח: all non-Jews, who keep the seven מצוות
An animal missing a limb
A private altar outside the Temple
You might have thought: the mistaken first idea
It comes to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, 'מכל אלה' teaches that a blemished animal from a נכרי is not accepted in the Temple, even though בני נח may offer it on their own altar.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: it is needed
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'מיד בן נכר לא תקריבו... מכל אלה' (ויקרא 22:25).

phrases.english: it would enter your mind to say
since the descendants of Noah

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְצוִּּוין אֶלָּא עַל מְחוּסַּר אֵבֶר
phrases.english: are commanded only about an animal missing a limb
on their own altar
perhaps we too

that we do not accept them

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אִצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the רבנן use the פסוק that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה used for קבלה in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the פסוק a different necessary lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בני נח may offer animals with small blemishes, we could accept such animals from them
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מכל אלה' teaches that we do not accept any blemished animal from a נכרי

steps.title: ריש לקיש: maybe the איסור applies only to an animal that became blemished later
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש suggests that the ברייתא's איסור against consecrating a בעל מום may apply only to a תם that later became blemished. An animal blemished from birth is like a date palm, and consecrating it simply means consecrating its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש objected: Maybe the ברייתא only taught that a person transgresses when the animal was unblemished and then became blemished. If it was blemished from the start, it is just like a date palm.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. ריש לקיש questions how far the earlier ברייתא reaches. That ברייתא said that someone who consecrates a בעל מום for the altar violates several לאוין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born with a blemish was never fit for the altar. So consecrating it is like consecrating a tree: everyone understands he means its money value, and that is allowed. Only an animal that was once fit and then became blemished might look like a real altar offering, so ריש לקיש limits the איסור to that case.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it: a strong challenge
An unblemished animal
A blemished animal, unfit for the altar
From the start, here meaning from birth
A date palm: something holy only for its value, never as an offering

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying a born-blemished animal cannot be consecrated at all. He is saying that consecrating it counts as consecrating its value, so there is no sin.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish objects to this
perhaps we learned it
phrases.notes: He's talking about the earlier ברייתא: someone who consecrates a blemished animal for the altar breaks several לאוין.

phrases.english: only about an unblemished animal that became blemished
and only then does he transgress
for if it was blemished from the start
it is just a date palm
phrases.notes: A tree can never be an offering, so consecrating it only means its value goes to the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: שֶׁמָּא לֹא שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about which blemished animals the earlier ברייתא covers
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's plain statement that consecrating any בעל מום violates לאוין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal blemished from birth was never fit for the altar, so consecrating it is like consecrating a tree, meaning for its value only. The איסור should therefore apply only to a תם that became blemished.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר יוסף: the פרשה mentions blemishes that exist from birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף answers that the פרשה of blemished offerings mentions שרוע וקלוט, an animal with a limb too long or too short. Those are blemishes an animal is born with, so the איסור covers born-blemished animals too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said to him: 'Too long or too short' is written in that פרשה, and these animals are blemished from birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר יוסף responds to ריש לקיש with a proof from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah's list of blemished animals that may not be offered includes blemishes found only from birth, then the איסור must include animals that were born blemished. That rejects ריש לקיש's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with one limb longer than its partner (too long)
An animal whose hooves are round and not split (the word the פסוק pairs with שָׂרוּעַ, often translated 'too short')
A Torah passage on one topic

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Yosef said to him
"too long or too short"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:23

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף: שָׂרוּעַ וְקָלוּט כְּתִיב בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's objection with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the פסוק that the איסור includes born blemishes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a תם that became blemished is included in the איסור
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרשה lists blemishes found from birth, so born-blemished animals are included

steps.title: ריש לקיש: maybe those פסוקים speak only about תמורה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rejects the proof. Maybe the born-blemish cases in the פרשה refer only to תמורה, which is stricter. A משנה says sanctity takes effect through תמורה even on an animal with a permanent blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש answered him: Maybe that was taught only about תמורה. As the משנה says: there is a stringency in תמורה over a regular offering, since sanctity takes effect through it even on an animal with a permanent blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back against רבי חייא בר יוסף's proof by limiting it to the case of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תמורה, a blemished animal swapped for a holy one becomes fully holy. With a regular הקדש, a born-blemished animal only becomes holy for its value. So perhaps the פסוק about שרוע וקלוט speaks only of תמורה, and regular consecration of a born-blemished animal is still like a date palm and carries no sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution: trying to swap a regular animal for a consecrated one, which makes both holy
A stringency: a way one thing is stricter than another
A permanent blemish
Sanctity takes effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between תמורה and regular consecration is the key to ריש לקיש's view. Real holiness can rest on a born-blemished animal through תמורה but not through regular הקדש.

phrases.english: He said to him
perhaps we learned it only about substitution
as we learned in a mishna
there is a stringency in a substitute over an offering
in that sanctity takes effect on it
even on an animal with a permanent blemish

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֶׁמָּא לֹא שָׁנִינוּ אֶלָּא בִּתְמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חייא בר יוסף's proof from שרוע וקלוט
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שרוע וקלוט does not apply to regular consecration
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The born-blemish cases may refer only to תמורה, where sanctity takes effect even on a permanent בעל מום

steps.title: Five prohibitions, not six, so the case is not about תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי ינאי: the חכמים voted that one who consecrates a בעל מום for the מזבח breaks five prohibitions. If the case involved תמורה, there would be six, because תמורה has its own לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: Didn't you hear what רבי ינאי said? The חכמים took a vote in a group and decided: someone who consecrates a blemished animal for the מזבח breaks five separate prohibitions. If this were also about תמורה, there would be six, since there is also the לאו of תמורה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back against ריש לקיש's claim that the born-blemish cases are only about תמורה. He uses a known count of five prohibitions to prove that the case is not about תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said in step 24 that the born-blemish cases in the פרשה might refer only to תמורה. But the חכמים counted exactly five prohibitions for consecrating a בעל מום. If תמורה were part of the case, its own לאו would make six, so the five must apply to ordinary consecration, even of an animal blemished from birth.

keyTerms.meaning: They sat as a group, counted votes, and decided
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought on the מזבח
Five separate prohibitions (literally, 'five names')
The negative commandment against swapping a קרבן for another animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
phrases.notes: He's speaking to ריש לקיש, answering his rejection from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Didn't you hear that which Rabbi Yannai said:
In a group they voted and concluded:
One who consecrates a blemished animal for the altar
violates five separate prohibitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's rejection in step 24 by showing the case cannot be about תמורה.
steps.raayaObject: The איסור against consecrating a בעל מום applies to plain consecration, not only to תמורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי's report that the חכמים counted five prohibitions, not six.

steps.title: Why give מלקות for an animal blemished from birth?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks: if the case really is about an animal blemished from birth, why is the person lashed? Consecrating it is just like consecrating a date palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that this is about an animal blemished from the start? Why should he get lashes? It is just like a date palm!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש accepts that the case is not about תמורה, but asks a logical question about the result. He does not see why someone would get מלקות for consecrating an animal that was blemished from birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's point from step 22 comes back. An animal blemished from birth was never fit for the מזבח, so consecrating it only gives its money value to הקדש, just like consecrating a tree. Nobody is lashed for consecrating a date palm, so why here?

keyTerms.meaning: An animal blemished from the start, from birth
He receives lashes (מלקות)
A date palm

phrases.english: Rather, what? It is about an animal blemished from the outset?
phrases.notes: Now ריש לקיש is speaking, going along with the 'not תמורה' point for argument's sake.

phrases.english: Why is he flogged?
It is merely a date palm!
phrases.notes: Like consecrating a tree, it only gives its value to הקדש; it was never fit to be a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אַמַּאי לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבי יוחנן's proof about the case, then challenges the logic of giving מלקות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one is lashed for consecrating an animal blemished from birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such an animal was never fit for the מזבח, so consecrating it is only consecrating its value, like a date palm, which carries no מלקות.

steps.title: A blemished animal is a disgrace; a date palm is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a date palm is a kind of wood, so consecrating it is not disgraceful. But consecrating a blemished animal is a disgrace: he skipped unblemished animals and chose blemished ones, so he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A date palm is not a disgraceful thing; it is a type of wood. But a blemished animal from the start is a disgraceful thing. Since he passed over perfect animals and consecrated blemished ones, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the date palm comparison fails. The difference is that consecrating a blemished animal is an insult to the מזבח, while a tree is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood is actually used on the מזבח, so giving a date palm to הקדש is respectful. Animals do come as קרבנות, and choosing a flawed one when perfect ones exist looks down on the מזבח. That disgrace is the reason for מלקות, even if the animal was never fit.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disgraceful, degrading thing
A type of wood
Unblemished, perfect animals
He is liable (here, to מלקות)

steps.whatToRemember: The reason for מלקות on a born-blemished animal is that it is a disgrace to choose a flawed animal over perfect ones.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: A date palm is not a disgraceful matter,
it is a type of wood;
phrases.notes: Wood is burned on the מזבח, so giving a tree to הקדש is no insult.

phrases.english: an animal blemished from the outset is a disgraceful matter,
since he passed over unblemished animals
and consecrated blemished ones, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּיקְלָא לָאו זִילָא מִילְּתָא מִין עֵצִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question by showing how the date palm is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a blemished animal is disgraceful, a date palm is not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A born-blemished animal is like a date palm, so no מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Choosing a blemished animal over perfect ones is a disgrace, so he gets מלקות.

steps.title: Second version: a date palm has no fit kind, an animal does
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי יוחנן says that even so, consecrating a blemished animal is a disgrace. A date palm has nothing of its kind that is fit as a קרבן, so there are no lashes. A blemished animal does have fit animals of its kind, so there are lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: He said to him: Even so, it is a disgraceful thing. A date palm, since nothing of its kind is brought, he is not lashed. That leaves out a blemished animal: since there is something of its kind that is brought, he is lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to word רבי יוחנן's answer. The point is still disgrace, but the focus is whether the same kind of item can be a fit קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference is not that wood is used on the מזבח. It is that no date palm is ever a קרבן, so nothing better was passed over. Animals of the same kind can be perfect קרבנות, so choosing a blemished one is an insult.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the statement
It is a degrading, shameful matter
Of its own kind
To exclude, which leaves out

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that disgrace is the reason. They only differ in why a date palm is not a disgrace: in the first version because wood is used on the מזבח, in the second because no date palm is ever a קרבן.

phrases.english: Another version: He said to him:
Even so, the matter is disgraceful,
for a date palm, since nothing of its kind is offered, he is not flogged,
which excludes a blemished animal:
since there is something of its kind that is offered, he is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי בַּזְיָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second wording of רבי יוחנן's answer from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether a fit item of the same kind exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A born-blemished animal is like a date palm, so no מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since perfect animals of the same kind exist, choosing a blemished one is a disgrace and brings מלקות.

steps.title: Lashes even when consecrating for the money of נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says: now that the reason for lashes is that it is a disgrace, even someone who consecrates a blemished animal so its money can buy נסכים is lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that it has been said that the reason a blemished animal brings lashes is that it is disgraceful, even someone who consecrates it for the money of נסכים is also lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes רבי יוחנן's reason and applies it to a new case. He extends the מלקות to someone who consecrates a blemished animal to be sold for נסכים money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think there are no lashes when the animal is consecrated only for its value, since it will never go on the מזבח. But if the reason is disgrace, the very act of choosing a blemished animal for the מזבח's needs is shameful. So the lashes apply even here.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that the reason has been said
Money for buying wine libations (נסכים)

steps.whatToRemember: Since the reason for מלקות is disgrace, רבא rules that one is lashed even when a blemished animal is consecrated only for its value for נסכים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a reason (טעמא) can widen a הלכה: once we know why the איסור exists, it reaches cases the original rule did not mention.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that the reason has been stated
that for a blemished animal he is flogged
because the matter is disgraceful,
even if he consecrates it for the money for libations,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way it means 'consecrates.'

phrases.english: he is also flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דַּאֲמוּר טַעְמָא דְּבַעַל מוּם דְּלָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the disgrace reason from steps 27 and 28 to rule on a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who consecrates a blemished animal even for the money of נסכים receives מלקות, because the act itself is a disgrace.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא agrees with רבא's ruling about consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבא's view:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to quote a ברייתא that supports what רבא just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 29, רבא reasoned that the lashes come from the disgrace of consecrating a בעל מום. So even consecrating it to buy נסכים gets lashes. The phrase תניא כוותיה tells us a ברייתא backs him up, but the ברייתא's words only come next.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him; agreeing with his opinion
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
Wine libations poured with קרבנות

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rava:
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's ruling in Step 29 about consecrating a blemished animal for נסכים money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a ברייתא that supports רבא's ruling from Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that one who consecrates a בעל מום for its money to buy נסכים is lashed, because it is a disgrace.
